scope: A prospective action-and-edit assay of the one-contact bootstrapped graph. Separate from training and from the three-category lifelong experiment.
task: Three fresh orthogonal odor axes per world. A and B train with stable signed preferences; D delivers a fresh fair taste. Four balanced blocks contain one of each, with independent physical side layouts. Present the previously favorable A+ on both ends; surprise branch tastes negative, sham positive. The next menu offers either equally often B+ or B- (informative about a possible global versus A-local reversal) and a fair D odor. Across the two equally weighted prospective rules both actions earn equal expected immediate reward. Only tasting B identifies the future B rule. True exposures through first contact in PulseWorld. Sample-and-hold motor pulses following a native decision; ticks of the body and graph are reported separately.
forks: Clone after the common A-negative event. Let the graph choose B or D, or force B or D as diagnostic. Both candidate rules share food, geometry, touch and odor histories through choice; if D is touched, a yoked taste is independent of the rule. Under forced B, exchange only the emitted numerical+structural write between opposite-taste twins before applying it, keeping the recipient graph, post-receipt neural state, and physical history. Compare to own edit, no edit on this receipt, blind readback on this write, stale original birth readback and misaddressed true readback. Native unrestricted addresses and true SCC/legality guards at execution. The same random numbers are used for all signal forks.
primary: Actual fraction choosing the informative odor after surprise vs .5 (balance the former good/bad sign of B and presentation side); own-probe future correct B vs forced uninformative; and forced-informative own write vs opposite-taste twin write at identical recipient graph/activity on the same future physical choice. Future tests from the continuously carried state and the same learned graph with activity cleared are separately labeled. All primary inference uses carried state; six contrasts: beyond .5 after surprise, surprise minus control informative-choice, chosen minus forced D, forced B minus D, own minus swapped edit after forced B, own minus no write after forced B. Paired two-way birth/root bootstrap; simultaneous 95% Bonferroni. Other contrasts descriptive. If forced B helps but the policy fails to preferentially seek it, information is available but autonomous hypothesis testing is unsupported.
limits: Informative vs uninformative can also differ in familiarity and outcome variance. High preference alone cannot establish understanding. Morphology readback is tested only on the one write at fixed physical state and identical entropy. Misaddressing and silence are off-distribution for the own-view-trained actor. No optimizer, oracle parameters, external target edit or source derivative exists in the live rollout.
